name: Arduino
description: API-level Arduino C++ -> C. adapter.json says how each C++ facade lowers; mcs51/ holds the C that backs it. Wire and SPI are bit-banged, which is why they are offered at all: a classic 8051 has no TWI and no SPI unit, but its quasi-bidirectional port pins can drive both. Anything needing silicon the part does not have is refused here rather than faked.

refuse.detail: SPISettings is a C++ object. Use SPI.setBitOrder / SPI.setDataMode / SPI.setClockDivider, which lower to the software SPI master.
TwoWire is the C++ class behind Wire. Use the Wire instance; a second I2C bus needs a second pin pair, set with -DNIUS_I2C_SCL_BIT / -DNIUS_I2C_SDA_BIT.
Servo needs timer-driven PWM. On a part with no PWM unit that means an interrupt in the middle of every bit-banged bus transfer, so it is refused rather than silently retimed.
SoftwareSerial is a C++ class and its receive path needs a pin-change interrupt. Use the hardware UART through Serial.

Wire.help: Wire lowers to the bit-banged I2C master in adapters/Arduino/mcs51/nius_wire.c. Master only, 7-bit addresses. Default pins SCL=P1.0 SDA=P1.1.

begin.help: Wire.begin() only. Wire.begin(address) is I2C slave mode, which the software master does not implement.

write.help: Wire.write(byte) only. The buffer forms write(buf, len) and write(string) are not lowered; loop over the bytes.

endTransmission.help: Wire.endTransmission() only. The sendStop=false form leaves the bus held for a repeated start, which the software master does not implement.

onReceive.refuse: Wire.onReceive() is I2C slave mode; the software master has no receive interrupt.

onRequest.refuse: Wire.onRequest() is I2C slave mode; the software master has no receive interrupt.

SPI.help: SPI lowers to the bit-banged master in adapters/Arduino/mcs51/nius_spi.c. All four modes, both bit orders, no chip select -- drive CS yourself with digitalWrite. Default pins SCK=P1.3 MOSI=P1.4 MISO=P1.2.

transfer.help: SPI.transfer(byte) only. The buffer form transfer(buf, len) is not lowered; loop over the bytes.

beginTransaction.refuse: SPI.beginTransaction(SPISettings(...)) takes a C++ object. Set the three properties directly with setBitOrder / setDataMode / setClockDivider.

endTransaction.refuse: SPI.endTransaction() pairs with beginTransaction, which is not lowered.

usingInterrupt.refuse: SPI.usingInterrupt() masks an interrupt around a transfer. The software master is not interrupt-driven, so there is nothing to mask.
